## Session: 2026-05-15 round 15 (Phase F — Bug #5 follow-up: account-deletion cascade gaps)
### Task Completed: F-DELETE-CASCADE-WAVE2 — `deleteAllForUser` now also erases `fcmTokens` + sender-side `shareInvites`; `firestore.rules` billing block lets the owner delete proStatus for DSGVO erasure

### Layer: Phase F. Verification + partial completion of Cowork's Bug #5 work (simplified user report — "account deletion doesn't actually delete / DSGVO violation").

### Context:
User asked to verify Cowork's Bug #5 fix. Core fix verified CORRECT: `deleteAllForUser` runs BEFORE `FirebaseUser.delete()`, awaited via callback (SettingsDialogFragment:1007-1036); 9 collections cascaded (plants+cover.jpg, reminders, photos+Storage, rooms, memos, vacation, streak, challenges, proStatus); failure handling logs + proceeds.

**Gaps found** — the fix's Javadoc claimed "nothing else is per-user-keyed outside users/{uid}/", which is false. Wave 2 Family Share added three collections the app writes:
- `users/{uid}/fcmTokens/*` — written by FcmTokenManager.kt:60; rules themselves call these "personally identifying". NOT cascaded. Client CAN delete (rule: `read, delete: if isOwner`).
- `/shareInvites/*` (top-level) — written by ShareInviteManager.createInvite; carry `fromEmail` + `toEmail` (third-party PII). NOT cascaded. Client can delete only sender-side (`fromUid == uid`).
- `users/{uid}/sharedPlants/*` — rule `write: if false`; client cannot delete at all.

**Conflict found** — `proStatusDocRef(uid).delete()` would be DENIED once Bug #10's `billing: write:if false` rule deploys. The Bug #10 rule comment wrongly claimed `deleteAllForUser` "uses the admin-SDK ... bypasses these rules" — but it is an Android client-SDK method.

### Fix (section A — client-side + rules file; section B deferred to a Cloud Function):
- `FirebaseSyncManager.deleteAllForUser`: added cascade steps for `fcmTokens` (whole collection) and `shareInvites where fromUid == uid`. Widened `deleteAllDocsInCollection` to accept `Query` (CollectionReference is-a Query — existing callers unchanged) so the filtered shareInvites query reuses the same helper. Added `fcmTokensRef(uid)` shortcut. Corrected the Javadoc's false "out of scope" claim and documented the CF-only remainder.
- `firestore.rules` billing block: `allow write: if false` → `allow create, update: if false; allow delete: if isOwner(userId);`. Preserves Bug #10 anti-tampering (client still can't fake isPro) while unblocking the Bug #5 DSGVO erasure. Corrected the stale comment that claimed deleteAllForUser bypasses rules.

### Evidence:
  - Files changed: `app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/FirebaseSyncManager.java`, `firestore.rules`
  - `grep -n "fcmTokens\|shareInvites" FirebaseSyncManager.java` → cascade now references both
  - `grep -n "allow delete" firestore.rules` → billing block now has owner delete
  - Acceptance criteria:
    - [✅] fcmTokens cascaded — client rule permits owner delete
    - [✅] sender-side shareInvites cascaded — client rule permits `fromUid` delete
    - [✅] billing rule no longer blocks the client-side GDPR delete; create/update still denied
    - [⏳] recipient-side shareInvites (`toUid == uid`) + `users/{uid}/sharedPlants/*` — CF required, see section B

### Task Completed: F-GUEST-PROMOTE-CHILD-REKEY — `promoteGuestRowsToUser` now re-keys the OWN primary keys of guest reminders/photos/memos, not just their `plantId` FK

### Layer: Phase F. Verification + completion of Cowork's Bug #4 work (simplified user report — "guest who signs in later loses plants").

### Context:
User asked to verify Cowork's Bug #4 fix. The plant-level collision was genuinely fixed (marker trick bumps `plant`'s `sqlite_sequence` to 1,000,000; `Plant.id` confirmed `@PrimaryKey(autoGenerate=true)`; `GUEST_EMAIL_VALUE` confirmed == `AuthRepository.GUEST_EMAIL`).

**Gap found:** the fix re-keyed only the PLANT. Guest reminders/photos/memos kept their OWN autogen PKs — only their `plantId` FK was re-pointed via `dao.update(...)`. All three children are `@PrimaryKey(autoGenerate=true)` and round-trip their explicit `id` through Firestore (`WateringReminder.id` etc. are public, no `@Exclude`; `onRemindersImported` does not zero them). So a guest reminder id=5 still collided with the cloud account's reminder id=5 on import → `@Insert` ABORT (reminder/memo) or REPLACE (photo) → silent loss of the cloud account's children / overwrite of the guest's photos. The fix's own comment (MainActivity.java ~884) names this exact "Same loss for ReminderDao + JournalMemoDao" failure but only closed it for plants.

### Fix (MainActivity.java `promoteGuestRowsToUser`):
- Step 1 now bumps `sqlite_sequence` on all FOUR tables (plant + reminder + plant_photo + journal_memo) via one marker row each. Child markers carry `plantId = OFFSET` (FK to the plant marker, inserted first); markers deleted child-first, plant-marker-last.
- Step 2 children are now re-INSERTED with `id=0` (fresh autogen PK ≥ OFFSET+1) instead of `update`-d in place. Original child rows (still pointing at `oldId`) are swept by the existing FK CASCADE when the old guest plant is deleted.
- `JournalMemoDao.insert` returns the new rowid → written back via `m.setId(...)` because `syncJournalMemo` keys the Firestore doc on `memo.getId()` and skips `id <= 0`. `ReminderDao.insert` is void and `syncReminder` keys on `plantId+"_"+date` (not `reminder.id`), so leaving reminder `id=0` is harmless.

### Evidence:
  - File changed: `app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/MainActivity.java` (`promoteGuestRowsToUser` + REKEY_AUTOGEN_OFFSET javadoc + call-site comment)
  - DAO signatures verified: `PlantPhotoDao.insert` → `long` (REPLACE), `JournalMemoDao.insert` → `Long` (ABORT), `ReminderDao.insert` → `void` (ABORT)
  - Entities verified all `@PrimaryKey(autoGenerate=true)` with FK CASCADE to Plant: Plant.java, WateringReminder.java, PlantPhoto.java, JournalMemo.kt
  - Acceptance criteria:
    - [✅] guest children get OWN PKs ≥ OFFSET+1 → cannot collide with cloud children
    - [✅] re-key wrapped in the existing `runInTransaction` — partial failure rolls back
    - [✅] FK ordering safe: plant inserted before its children; old rows cascade-swept on old-plant delete
    - [✅] memo new id written back for `syncJournalMemo`

### Build Status: ✅ `:app:compileDevDebugJavaWithJavac` passed (only the pre-existing deprecated-API note). Full `assembleProdRelease` not run this round — single-file Java change, compile verified.

### Regressions: none. Plant-level promote behavior unchanged; only the child path changed from update-in-place to re-insert.

### Next Task: User decision required (unchanged).

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 13 (Phase F — Bug #2 follow-up: storage.rules delete/read bug)
### Task Completed: F-STORAGE-RULES-VERBS — split `allow read, write` into `read, delete` + `create, update` in `storage.rules`

### Layer: Phase F. Verification of Cowork's Bug #2 work (simplified user report — "cloud rules not deployed").

### Context:
User asked to verify Cowork's Bug #2 fix. Two artifacts: `firestore.rules` + `storage.rules`. Deployment itself was correctly NOT done (sandbox can't auth to Firebase — logged honestly as a pending release blocker). `firestore.rules` verified correct: CS1 verb-split applied, all delete paths covered.

**`storage.rules` had a real bug** — same class as the CS1 bug it was meant to mirror:
```
allow read, write: if ... && request.resource.size < 8*1024*1024 && (request.resource == null || ...)
```
On `read` and `delete`, `request.resource` is null. `&&` evaluates left-to-right, so `request.resource.size` is touched BEFORE the null guard → rule errors → access denied. The null guard was placed only on the contentType check, not the size check. Net effect if deployed as-is: photo viewing AND cloud photo delete both 403.

### Fix:
Split the single `allow read, write` into:
- `allow read, delete: if auth + uid` — no `request.resource` access.
- `allow create, update: if auth + uid + size < 8MB + contentType image/*` — these carry `request.resource`.
Mirrors `firestore.rules` verb-split exactly.

### Evidence:
  - File changed: `storage.rules` (lines ~23-50)
  - `grep -n "allow read, delete\|allow create, update" storage.rules` → 1 hit each
  - `grep -n "allow read, write" storage.rules` → 0 hits (the broken shape is gone)
  - Acceptance criteria:
    - [✅] no rule expression touches `request.resource.*` on a read/delete path
    - [✅] size + MIME guards retained on create/update
    - [⏳] needs confirmation in Firebase Console → Rules Playground before deploy (static analysis only — sandbox can't run the rules emulator)

### Build Status: N/A — rules file only, no Android/Kotlin/Java changed.

### Regressions: none. Create/update behavior (size cap + image-only MIME) is byte-equivalent to before.

### Still outstanding (Fady's hands — unchanged from prior rounds):
  - `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,storage:rules` — NOT done. Needs `firebase use <project-id>` first (no `.firebaserc` in repo).

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 12 (Phase F — Bug #10: server-side Pro verification)
### Task Completed: F-PRO-VERIFY-SERVER — Cloud Function `verifyPurchase` cross-checks every purchase against Google Play Developer API; client `BillingManager` routes all Pro grants through it; Firestore rule on `users/{uid}/billing/proStatus` becomes write-only-via-admin-SDK
### Layer: Phase F (functional / security). Simplified user report Bug #10. DEFERRED_ISSUES #17.

### Bug:
Pre-fix `BillingManager.onPurchasesUpdated` trusted the local Google Play Billing SDK callback. A rooted device with Lucky Patcher (or any billing emulator app) intercepts the callback and injects a forged "PURCHASED" state — granting permanent Pro with no payment. Industry-standard fix is server-side validation against Play Developer API.

### Files changed:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `functions/src/index.ts` | new `verifyPurchase` callable + `defineSecret("PLAY_SA_KEY")` + `googleapis` import + ~150 lines |
| `functions/package.json` | added `"googleapis": "^144.0.0"` dep |
| `app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/billing/BillingManager.kt` | new `grantProWithVerification(purchases)` chokepoint + `verifyOnePurchaseWithCloud(...)` callable wrapper + `productTypeFor(sku)` mapping; 3 grant sites rewritten |
| `app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/billing/ProStatusManager.kt` | removed the `FirebaseSyncManager.syncProStatus(...)` mirror call from `setPro` (the new Firestore rule denies it; only the CF can write) |
| `firestore.rules` | `users/{uid}/billing/{docId}` → `read: owner; write: false` (admin SDK bypass writes from CF) |
| `BUG10_MANUAL_SETUP.md` (new, repo root) | step-by-step manual setup for Fady (~150 lines): SA creation, Play Console grant, secret upload, deploy, verification, cost expectations, rollback |

### Cloud Function semantics:
- HTTPS callable. Body: `{ productId, purchaseToken, productType: "subs" | "inapp" }`. Returns `{ verified, isPro, reason? }`.
- Loads SA key from `PLAY_SA_KEY` Cloud Secret Manager secret.
- Calls `androidpublisher.purchases.subscriptions.get` (SUBS) or `purchases.products.get` (INAPP).
- SUBS valid iff `expiryTimeMillis > now` AND `paymentState in (1,2)`.
- INAPP valid iff `purchaseState === 0`.
- Writes verified state to `users/{uid}/billing/proStatus` with admin SDK.
- Doesn't store `purchaseToken` in Firestore (secret; expanding blast radius).
- On secret missing/malformed: logs `server_misconfigured` + returns `verified=false`. Client falls back to optimistic local grant — matches pre-Bug-#10 UX, no security regression vs. pre-fix.

### Android side semantics:
`grantProWithVerification(purchases)`:
- Walks each PURCHASED purchase; calls CF for each.
- ANY verified → setPro(true).
- ALL explicitly rejected (no transient failures) → setPro(false).
- Mix of transient failures → optimistic setPro(true) (CF wrote nothing to Firestore in transient case; cloud reflects previous state).
- Three call sites updated: `onPurchasesUpdated` (post-purchase), `restorePurchases` (manual restore), `refreshPurchases` (connect-time check).

### Cross-device sync trade-off (acknowledged):
Pre-fix: phone purchase → tablet sees Pro within seconds (Firestore listener via the now-removed cloud mirror). Post-fix: tablet sees Pro on its NEXT app launch (when its own `connect()` runs `verifyPurchase` for any cached Play purchase). Latency goes from "seconds" to "next launch on the other device". Acceptable for an anti-fraud mechanism, and the OLD path was security-disqualifying anyway.

### Verification (static — sandbox can't run gradle / npm / firebase deploy):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `verifyPurchase` callable defined in CF | ✅ |
| Android: 3 grant sites + 2 helpers + 1 productType mapping wired | ✅ |
| ProStatusManager.setPro no longer calls syncProStatus | ✅ (`grep -n "syncProStatus" ProStatusManager.kt` → 0) |
| Firestore rule denies client writes on /billing | ✅ (`allow write: if false`) |
| `googleapis` in package.json | ✅ |
| Manual setup doc exists | ✅ (BUG10_MANUAL_SETUP.md) |

### Standing CLAUDE.md regression sweep:

| Metric | Before | After | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `YOUR_API_KEY_HERE` | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| AdMob test ids | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| DAO in UI (C2) | 4 | 4 | ✅ |
| `getEmail()` (A1) | 8 | 8 | ✅ |
| `new Thread()` | 3 | 3 | ✅ |
| `catch (X ignored)` | 2 | 2 | ✅ |

### Build Status: ⏳ deferred to local machine. Three builds needed:
1. `cd functions && npm install && npm run build` — TypeScript compile of `verifyPurchase` + `googleapis` import.
2. `firebase deploy --only functions,firestore:rules` — pushes CF + new rule.
3. `./gradlew :app:assembleProdRelease` — Android side.

### Manual setup required (full step-by-step in `BUG10_MANUAL_SETUP.md`):
1. Create service account `plantcare-play-verifier` in Google Cloud Console.
2. Grant it "View financial data" in Google Play Console → API access.
3. Download SA key JSON.
4. `firebase functions:secrets:set PLAY_SA_KEY < /path/to/key.json`.
5. Deploy + License-Tester verification.

Until step 4 is done, `verifyPurchase` returns `{ verified: false, reason: "server_misconfigured" }` for every call. Android client gracefully degrades to optimistic local grant — same UX as pre-Bug-#10. No regression risk shipping the round without the secret set.

### Next Task: Stop and ship. We've covered all 10 simplified-report items (round 7 was net-zero by design — feature already shipped). Build + manual setup + device test cycle is the right next step before adding more code.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 10 (Phase F — Bug #9: NotificationChannel v2 migration)
### Task Completed: F-NOTIF-CHANNEL-V2 — minted `plant_care_reminders_v2` channel + cascade-delete of legacy `plant_care_reminders` so existing users actually get the IMPORTANCE_HIGH the N4 fix intended

### Layer: Phase F (functional). Simplified user report Bug #9. DEFERRED_ISSUES #8.

### Pre-flight grep (rounds 7 + 8 lessons applied):
- `CHANNEL_ID = "plant_care_reminders"` declared in `PlantNotificationHelper.java:24`.
- Importance already set to `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` (per the prior N4 fix) — but only NEW installs / fresh-data wipes ever felt it. Android caches the original IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT for users who installed before N4 landed.
- 5 caller sites use the constant `PlantNotificationHelper.CHANNEL_ID`:
  - `PlantNotificationHelper.java:47` (channel creation)
  - `PlantNotificationHelper.java:103, 136, 177` (3 NotificationCompat.Builder sites — morning, evening, weather-shift)
  - `PlantCareMessagingService.kt:67` (FCM share-invite notification)
- One additional touchpoint outside Java: `functions/src/index.ts:137` — the share-invite Cloud Function sets `channelId: "plant_care_reminders"` in its FCM android config. Needed updating too, otherwise pushes from the CF would target the deleted legacy channel.

### Bug:

| Tag | File(s) | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-NOTIF-CHANNEL-V2** | `PlantNotificationHelper.java` (constant + createNotificationChannel) + `functions/src/index.ts` (FCM channelId) | **Stale-channel-importance** | Android's `NotificationManager.createNotificationChannel(...)` is "create-or-leave-alone" semantics: passing a NEW channel definition for an existing channel id silently keeps the OLD definition. The N4 fix changed the code to IMPORTANCE_HIGH but couldn't change the runtime channel for users whose channel was created at IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT. They permanently get silent reminders unless they manually toggle the channel in system settings — which most users never do. |

### Fix:

**1. Mint a new channel id (PlantNotificationHelper.java):**
- `CHANNEL_ID` (the symbol) keeps its name; only its VALUE moves to `"plant_care_reminders_v2"`. All 5 caller sites that reference `PlantNotificationHelper.CHANNEL_ID` automatically pick up the new value with zero edits.
- New private constant `CHANNEL_ID_LEGACY = "plant_care_reminders"` — used ONLY inside `createNotificationChannel` to delete the orphaned legacy channel. Never used to post.

**2. Update `createNotificationChannel`:**
- Creates the v2 channel as before (same name/description strings, same IMPORTANCE_HIGH, same vibration enabled).
- ALSO calls `manager.deleteNotificationChannel(CHANNEL_ID_LEGACY)`. Idempotent — Android silently succeeds when deleting a non-existent channel id, so devices that never had the legacy channel (fresh installs) just see a no-op. Wrapped in try/catch with `CrashReporter.log` so a system-level NotificationManager failure here can't block the primary `createNotificationChannel` above.

**3. Update Cloud Function FCM target (functions/src/index.ts):**
- `android.notification.channelId` changed from `"plant_care_reminders"` to `"plant_care_reminders_v2"` in the share-invite push payload. Keeps share-invite pushes inside the same channel as watering reminders so users get a single, unified user-controlled notification category — no separate permission re-prompt for share invites.

### Why migrate the constant value rather than rename the symbol:
The 5 caller sites all reference `PlantNotificationHelper.CHANNEL_ID`. If I had renamed the constant to `CHANNEL_ID_V2`, every caller would need editing AND the migration history would be obscured (the symbol name carries no signal about which version it points to). Keeping `CHANNEL_ID` as the symbol means future callers don't need to know there ever was a migration — they just use "the channel id" and get the current one.

### When does the migration happen at runtime:
`createNotificationChannel(context)` is called on every notification post (lines 83 + 124 of PlantNotificationHelper) AND from a few other entry points. The PlantReminderWorker fires every ~6 hours — so within that window of upgrading, every user has the v2 channel created and the legacy one deleted. No app-launch-only gate, no user-action requirement, no retry logic needed.

### Verification (static):

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Constant value migrated | `grep -n "CHANNEL_ID = \"" PlantNotificationHelper.java` | `CHANNEL_ID = "plant_care_reminders_v2"` (line 47) ✅ |
| Legacy id retained for delete only | `grep -n "CHANNEL_ID_LEGACY" PlantNotificationHelper.java` | declared once (line 55) + used once in deleteNotificationChannel call ✅ |
| `deleteNotificationChannel` wired in createNotificationChannel | `grep -n "deleteNotificationChannel" PlantNotificationHelper.java` | 1 hit, inside the createNotificationChannel body, wrapped in try/catch ✅ |
| All 5 callers continue to use the symbol (no edits needed) | `grep -rn "PlantNotificationHelper.CHANNEL_ID\|new NotificationCompat.Builder.*CHANNEL_ID" app/src/main/java` | 5 hits across 2 files (PlantNotificationHelper × 4 + PlantCareMessagingService × 1) ✅ |
| `plant_care_reminders` literal occurs ONLY in legacy-cleanup contexts | `grep -rn "plant_care_reminders\"" app/src/main/java` | 4 hits: 1 constant (CHANNEL_ID_LEGACY) + 3 in comments. **Zero live channel posts target the legacy id** ✅ |
| Cloud Function FCM channel updated | `grep -n "channelId" functions/src/index.ts` | `channelId: "plant_care_reminders_v2"` ✅ |

### Standing CLAUDE.md regression sweep:

| Metric | Pre-round-10 | Post-round-10 | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `YOUR_API_KEY_HERE` | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| AdMob test ids | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| DAO in UI (C2) | 4 | 4 | ✅ |
| `getEmail()` (A1) | 8 | 8 | ✅ |
| `new Thread()` | 3 | 3 | ✅ |
| `catch (X ignored)` | 2 | 2 | ✅ |

### Build Status: ⏳ deferred to local machine.

### Regressions: none.
- Symbol name unchanged → 5 caller sites are byte-identical to pre-round-10.
- Channel string resources (`notif_channel_name`, `notif_channel_description`) are unchanged — the rendered category name in system settings stays the same.
- `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`, vibration enabled, channel description — all preserved.
- The `try { ... } catch (Throwable t) { CrashReporter.INSTANCE.log(t); }` wrapper around the legacy delete is the only new error-handling — failures there don't propagate (intentional: a system-level failure here must not block the primary channel creation).

### Behavior change to verify on device:

**Path 1 — pre-N4 user upgrading to this build:**
1. Install a build with channel created at IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT (i.e. roll back to a version before N4 landed if you have one — otherwise simulate by setting IMPORTANCE_LOW manually in system settings).
2. Upgrade to the current build via Play Store / `adb install -r`.
3. Wait for the next PlantReminderWorker tick (or trigger one manually via WorkManager debug).
4. **Pre-fix:** notification still arrives silent; channel in Settings > Notifications still shows "Default" priority.
5. **Post-fix:** notification arrives with sound + heads-up display; system settings shows the OLD `plant_care_reminders` category disappeared (Android removed it via `deleteNotificationChannel`) and the new `plant_care_reminders_v2` category appears with the same visible name (because the user-facing name string is identical) at "High" priority.

**Path 2 — fresh install (no legacy channel ever existed):**
1. Install fresh on a wiped device.
2. Trigger any notification.
3. Channel `plant_care_reminders_v2` is created at IMPORTANCE_HIGH; `deleteNotificationChannel("plant_care_reminders")` is a no-op.
4. User sees a single channel in system settings, "High" priority, named per `notif_channel_name`. No trace of the legacy id ever existed for this user.

**Path 3 — share-invite push (Cloud Function path):**
1. Owner adds a recipient (Family Share Phase 1A → Cloud Function 1 → FCM push).
2. Push arrives on recipient's device. Pre-fix: targeted the legacy channel id which was deleted on this device on first Worker tick post-upgrade — the push would land "ungrouped" (Android's fallback channel). Post-fix: targets `plant_care_reminders_v2` directly → grouped under the same category as watering reminders.

### Manual deploys required from Fady:
- **Android:** `./gradlew :app:assembleProdRelease` builds the channel-rename. Standard release.
- **Cloud Function:** `cd functions && npm install && npm run build && firebase deploy --only functions`. Without this step, the share-invite push from `onShareInviteCreated` will continue targeting the legacy `plant_care_reminders` id — pushes still arrive (Android falls back to the "Other" category) but they won't be grouped with the watering reminders.

### Rollback plan (in case the migration causes a surprise):
- Revert PlantNotificationHelper.java + functions/src/index.ts to pre-round-10 state.
- Existing users keep the v2 channel even after rollback (Android doesn't auto-delete channels). Their notifications will silently stop firing (post-rollback the code targets the legacy id which Android then re-creates — at IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT). Users who installed during the round-10 window will permanently have the v2 channel as a stale category in system settings. Net cost of rollback: a confused-channel-list situation, fixable by app-data wipe or by re-applying round-10. **Recommendation:** ship round-10, observe for 1 week before considering rollback.

### Next Task: User decision required.
- **Option A:** Stop here. We have rounds 2-10 (9 functional fixes + 1 cleanup). Bug #10 (Pro server-side verification) is the only one left from the simplified report — needs a Cloud Function epic + Firestore rules expansion + ~2 days of work. Worth pausing to validate everything else before expanding.
- **Option B:** Bug #10 immediately. ~2 days of work. Adds resilience against modded APKs faking Pro purchases. Only matters once you start seeing them in the wild — not a launch blocker.
- **Option C:** Light Phase 6 (delivery state badge in PlantDetailDialog's share dialog) — the cosmetic round-6 follow-up I deferred. ~30 min.

I recommend **Option A** — we now have nine rounds of fixes ready to ship. Building, deploying rules + functions, and running the on-device test matrix is now its own significant work. Adding more before validating any of it would amplify the rollback radius if anything turns out to be subtly broken.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 8 (Phase F — Bug #8: vacation taps must not burn streak)
### Task Completed: F-VACATION-TAP-SUPPRESS — Today-screen mark-watered taps + Mark-All-Watered notification action are now no-ops during an active vacation window
### Layer: Phase F (functional / UX). Simplified user report Bug #8. DEFERRED_ISSUES #7. User-facing pre-fix symptom: TodayFragment shows the "Du bist im Urlaubs-Modus" banner during an active vacation but leaves the reminder list fully tappable. A user who taps "done" out of habit (the banner is below the list, often missed) marks reminders complete that they didn't actually do, advances `wateredBy`, and increments their streak. On return, the streak claims they watered every day they were away — which is wrong.

### Pre-existing infrastructure (verified by grep BEFORE writing any code, learning from round-7):
- `VacationPrefs.isVacationActive(ctx, email, today=LocalDate.now())` — already exists, used by 6 callers (Worker, TodayViewModel, etc.). Returns true iff `start <= today <= end`. Java-friendly `@JvmStatic`.
- `PlantReminderWorker.java:142` — already gates Worker-driven notifications with `VacationPrefs.isVacationActive`. So the Worker doesn't POST notifications during vacation. The gap is for notifications POSTED before vacation started + still in the system shade, AND for direct UI taps from TodayFragment.

### Bug:

| Tag | File(s) | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-VACATION-TAP-SUPPRESS** | `DailyWateringAdapter.java` (3 mark-done sites) + `NotificationActionReceiver.java` (Mark-All-Watered loop) | **UX bug — vacation banner is informational only, taps still mutate state** | The vacation banner sits between the streak strip and the reminder list. Users who scroll past it and tap a reminder out of habit get the same `r.done = true; reminder.completedDate = new Date(); StreakBridge.onReminderMarkedDone(...)` flow as on a normal day. Net effect: their streak advances every day they're away, then snaps back to honesty when they return + miss a real day. The notification action has the same hazard via stale notifications in the shade. |

### Fix:

**1. New `isOnVacationNow()` helper in `DailyWateringAdapter`** (Java, ~17 lines): wraps `VacationPrefs.isVacationActive(context, userEmail, LocalDate.now())` with null-safety on `userEmail` (guest with stale state) and a defensive `try/catch` that fails OPEN — a corrupted vacation pref must NOT silently block legitimate taps forever. Logs to CrashReporter on the unlikely error path.

**2. Three guard sites in `DailyWateringAdapter`:**
- **Bulk water dialog** (`showBulkWaterDialog` at line ~185): guard at top, BEFORE the confirmation dialog opens. User gets immediate toast feedback that the action is intentionally inert, not a UI glitch.
- **Single-tap mark done** (line ~283): guard ONLY in the "not yet done → mark done" branch. The "done → un-mark" branch is allowed to pass — a user who accidentally marked a reminder done before vacation must be able to undo without restriction.
- **Reschedule-then-mark-done** (line ~514, "btnNo" of the overdue-reminder reschedule dialog): NO new guard needed. The reschedule dialog is reachable only through the single-tap path which is already gated above.

**3. One guard site in `NotificationActionReceiver`:** defensive guard inside the `BgExecutor.io` body, BEFORE the `getTodayAndOverdueRemindersForUserBlocking` query. Same fail-open pattern. The Worker normally prevents notifications from being posted during vacation, but a user who activated vacation AFTER a notification was already posted to the system shade can still tap the action — without this guard, that tap would burn the streak.

**Toast string** added to DE + EN: `vacation_tap_suppressed` ("Du bist im Urlaubs‑Modus — Aufgaben werden nicht gewertet." / "You're in vacation mode — tasks won't count."). Receiver doesn't toast (BroadcastReceiver context is process-level — toasts can crash on some Android versions); receiver just silently no-ops.

### Trade-offs intentionally accepted:
- **Reschedule-overdue is also blocked during vacation**, indirectly. Tapping an overdue reminder while on vacation now toasts and returns instead of opening the reschedule dialog. Rationale: during an active vacation, the user shouldn't be doing anything with reminders. Once `isVacationActive` returns false (vacation ended naturally OR was cleared from Settings), all flows behave normally — overdue reminders open the reschedule dialog as before.
- **Un-mark is always allowed.** A user who realizes they tapped "done" by accident before going on vacation can still un-mark. Vacation only blocks NEW done events, not corrections.
- **No setting to disable the guard.** The whole point is to protect against habitual taps; an opt-out would defeat the purpose. If a user genuinely wants to log a watering during vacation (e.g., they're house-sitting at a friend's), they can clear vacation mode in Settings, log the watering, then re-enable vacation.

### Verification (static — sandbox can't run gradle):

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Helper defined exactly once | `grep -n "isOnVacationNow" DailyWateringAdapter.java` | line 179 ✅ |
| Helper used in both bulk + single-tap paths | grep above | lines 200, 328 ✅ |
| Toast string in DE + EN | grep `vacation_tap_suppressed` | 2 hits (DE strings.xml + EN strings.xml) ✅ |
| Receiver guard present | `grep -n "VacationPrefs.isVacationActive" NotificationActionReceiver.java` | 1 hit, inside BgExecutor.io BEFORE the query loop ✅ |
| `TodayAdapter` (a separate, dead adapter) — left unguarded | `grep -rn "new TodayAdapter\|TodayAdapter(" app/src/main/java` | 0 caller hits — confirmed dead, not part of any user flow ✅ |
| Widget mark-watered (DEFERRED #15 — feature doesn't exist yet) | `grep -rn "done = true\|MARK_ALL_WATERED" app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/widget` | 0 hits — nothing to guard ✅ |

### Standing CLAUDE.md regression sweep:

| Metric | Pre-round-8 | Post-round-8 | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `YOUR_API_KEY_HERE` | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| AdMob test ids | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| DAO in UI (C2) | 4 | 4 | ✅ |
| `getEmail()` (A1) | 8 | 8 | ✅ |
| `new Thread()` | 3 | 3 | ✅ |
| `catch (X ignored)` | 2 | 2 | ✅ |

### Build Status: ⏳ deferred to local machine.

### Regressions: none.
- DailyWateringAdapter changes are additive: 1 new helper method + 2 inline guards (each 4 lines: if-toast-return).
- NotificationActionReceiver change is one inline guard at the top of the existing IO block.
- 1 new string in DE + 1 in EN — no name collision (verified by grep).
- No imports added (uses fully-qualified `com.example.plantcare.feature.vacation.VacationPrefs` + `android.widget.Toast` + `java.time.LocalDate`).
- No public API change; no schema change; no new dependencies.

### Behavior change to verify on device:
1. Go to Settings → Vacation mode → set start = today, end = today + 7 days. Save.
2. Open Today screen. The vacation banner appears.
3. Tap any pending reminder.
4. **Pre-fix:** reminder marks done, streak counter ticks up, notification dismisses.
5. **Post-fix:** toast "Du bist im Urlaubs-Modus — Aufgaben werden nicht gewertet" appears; reminder stays unmarked; streak unchanged.
6. Long-press a room header (the "mark all watered" gesture) → toast appears immediately, no confirmation dialog opens.
7. Pull down system shade. If a reminder notification was posted before vacation started, tap "Mark all watered" action. **Pre-fix:** all today's reminders flip done. **Post-fix:** silent no-op.
8. Cancel vacation in Settings (set both dates back, or use the "Clear" button). Today screen taps work normally again.
9. Bonus: tap a reminder that's ALREADY done while on vacation — should un-mark normally (vacation guard only blocks the not-done → done transition).

### Lesson reinforced:
The round-7 lesson (grep proactively before writing code) saved this round. I confirmed `VacationPrefs.isVacationActive` already existed before adding any new code, and confirmed `TodayAdapter` was a dead path before wasting time guarding it. Build won't have a "wait, this already exists" surprise.

### Next Task: User decision required.
- **Option A:** Bug #9 — NotificationChannel v2 migration. Existing users stuck on `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` after the Z2 fix; minting `plant_care_reminders_v2` makes the elevated importance reach them. Small change (~30 lines in PlantNotificationHelper + a one-time channel cleanup).
- **Option B:** Light cleanup — drop `app/src/main/plant_disease_model.tflite` (12 MB orphan, TFLite removed 2026-05-01) + remove "TensorFlow Lite (Apache 2.0)" line from `settings_help_licenses_body` in DE + EN strings.
- **Option C:** Stop here, ship a build, gather feedback on whether #9 is even hit by real users (depends on how many users installed before the channel-importance fix landed).
- **Option D:** Bug #10 (Pro server-side verification). MED priority but requires a Cloud Function epic + Firestore rules expansion + local verification flow rewrite. ~2 days of work; out of scope for a quick session.

I recommend **Option B** before Option A. The cleanup is 5-minute work that prevents a real bug — anyone who later moves the orphan tflite file back to `assets/` would re-add 12 MB to the APK with no functional benefit. Option A is meaningful but only matters for users who installed before late April and haven't reinstalled since — small population.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 6 (Phase F — Bug #6: complete Family Share end-to-end)
### Task Completed: F-FAMILY-SHARE-COMPLETE — finished the recipient-side half of the Wave 2 Family Share epic so the feature is no longer "owner sends invite into a void"
### Layer: Phase F (functional). DEFERRED_ISSUES.md #13. User-facing pre-fix state: owner could add an email to a plant's "share" list, the ShareInviteManager / FCM / Cloud Function chain delivered the invite to the recipient's device, the recipient could accept via the FCM push dialog — but after acceptance NOTHING happened on the recipient side: no plant card showed up, no "mark watered" button existed, no list of pending invites if the user missed the push, and removing someone via FamilyShareManager left them with full read access until they reinstalled. Net: the UI claimed sharing worked when in practice the recipient saw nothing.

### Inventory of what was already built (verified by grep — DO NOT redo):
- Cloud Functions: `onShareInviteCreated`, `onShareInviteAccepted`, `markSharedReminderWatered` callable.
- Android `FamilyShareManager.kt` — local CSV management of `Plant.sharedWith`.
- Android `ShareInviteManager.kt` — `createInvite`, `acceptInvite`, `declineInvite`, `markSharedReminderWatered` wrappers.
- Android `FcmTokenManager.kt` — token registration to `users/{uid}/fcmTokens/`.
- Android `PlantCareMessagingService.kt` — FCM receiver + notification builder.
- AndroidManifest — `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission + service registered.
- `firestore.rules` — `shareInvites` top-level + `users/{uid}/sharedPlants` + `users/{uid}/fcmTokens`.
- `PlantDetailDialogFragment` — already calls `ShareInviteManager.createInvite` from its share dialog.
- `MainActivity.handleSharePushIntent` — already shows accept/decline dialog from FCM tap.

### What was missing (this round's scope):
- Recipient-side data layer (no listener on `users/{uid}/sharedPlants/*` ever ran).
- Recipient-side UI (no screen displayed shared plants).
- Mark-watered routing (`markSharedReminderWatered` callable existed but no UI button called it).
- Pending-invites query for users who missed the FCM push (notification permission denied, app reinstalled, etc.).
- Revoke cascade (owner removing an email never deleted the cloud invite or the recipient's pointer doc).

### Phases:

**Phase 1A — Firestore rules expansion** (`firestore.rules`): added the `hasShareGrantFor(ownerId, plantId)` helper that checks the existence + `ownerUid` field of `users/{auth.uid}/sharedPlants/{plantId}`. Widened the read rules on `users/{userId}/plants/{plantId}` and `users/{userId}/reminders/{reminderId}` to allow recipients with an active grant. Reminder reads check `resource.data.plantId` so a recipient cannot enumerate the owner's other reminders. Writes remain owner-only — recipients use the `markSharedReminderWatered` callable for the only mutation they're allowed.

**Phase 1B — Cloud Function 4** (`functions/src/index.ts`): new `onShareInviteRevoked` triggered by document deletion on `shareInvites/{inviteId}`. Cascade-deletes the recipient's pointer doc at `users/{toUid}/sharedPlants/{plantId}` and pushes a `share_invite_revoked` data-only notification so the recipient's app can drop the plant card without waiting for the next listener tick.

**Phase 1C — `ShareInviteManager` Android additions**: `revokeInvite(inviteId, callback)` (deletes the Firestore invite doc, CF cascades), `findOpenInvitesByOwnerForPlant(ownerUid, plantId, callback)` (used by `FamilyShareManager.removeEmail` to locate the inviteId from the email — the per-plant CSV doesn't store inviteIds), `queryPendingInvitesForCurrentUser(callback)` (fetches `shareInvites where toEmail == currentUser.email AND status == "pending"` for the Settings screen), and a new `PendingInvite` DTO.

**Phase 2 — `SharedPlantsRepository.kt`** (new, ~210 lines): a singleton aggregator over the recipient's `sharedPlants` pointer collection. `start()` attaches a listener; for each pointer doc, attaches downstream listeners on the OWNER's `users/{ownerUid}/plants/{plantId}` doc + a `whereEqualTo("plantId", X)` query on the OWNER's reminders subcollection (the Phase 1A rule expansion makes these reads possible). Publishes a `LiveData<List<SharedPlantWithReminders>>` consumable by the UI. `stop()` removes all listeners + clears cache. `findSharedOwnerForReminder(reminderId)` exposes the cache for mark-watered routing.

**Phase 3 — dedicated `SharedPlantsActivity`** (new, ~155 lines): replaces the originally-planned deep integration into TodayFragment + MyPlantsFragment (Option α + X) with a dedicated screen reachable from Settings → "Mit mir geteilt". Single `RecyclerView` with multi-type `SharedPlantsAdapter` — three view types (HEADER, PENDING_INVITE, SHARED_PLANT). Sections: pending invitations on top (each with Accept / Decline buttons), active shared plants below (each with cover image + owner email + next-reminder text + Mark-Done button). `Activity.onStart` calls `SharedPlantsRepository.start()` + `refreshPendingInvites()`; `onStop` calls `SharedPlantsRepository.stop()` so background Firestore reads don't accumulate. Why a separate screen instead of inline integration: the Today + MyPlants refactor would have meant changes to `DailyWateringAdapter` (new item types), `TodayFragment` (LiveData merging), `TodayViewModel` (output reshaping), `MyPlantsFragment`, and at least 3 layouts — high-risk for a v1 of the feature. The user explicitly approved this scope reduction in mid-round.

**Phase 4 — Mark-watered routing** (in `SharedPlantsActivity` callbacks): tapping the "Done" button on a shared plant row routes through `ShareInviteManager.markSharedReminderWatered(ownerUid, reminderId.toString(), callback)`, which calls the `markSharedReminderWatered` Cloud Function. The CF re-validates the share grant + writes the watered status with admin privileges on the OWNER's reminder doc. The `reminders` listener in `SharedPlantsRepository` then ticks and the row updates locally.

**Phase 5 — Pending invites in Settings**: new entry-point card in `dialog_settings.xml` ("Mit mir geteilt" with subtitle + button) wired in `SettingsDialogFragment` to `startActivity(SharedPlantsActivity.class)`. The activity fetches pending invites via `queryPendingInvitesForCurrentUser` on each `onStart` so users who missed the FCM push can still see + accept invites.

**Phase 6 — DEFERRED**: per-email delivery-state badge ("⏳ Wird zugestellt", "📩 Wartet auf Registrierung", "✓ Zugestellt") in `PlantDetailDialogFragment.showShareDialog`. Out of scope for this round — purely cosmetic, doesn't affect functionality. String resources are added (`share_delivery_*`) so a follow-up can wire them in 30 min.

**Phase 7 — Revoke wiring** (`FamilyShareManager.removeEmail`): after the local CSV update, call new private helper `revokeOpenInvitesFor(plant, email)` which queries open invites via `findOpenInvitesByOwnerForPlant` and calls `revokeInvite` on each match. Cloud Function 4 (Phase 1B) cascades the rest. Also handled the `share_invite_revoked` push type in `MainActivity.handleSharePushIntent` — silent consumption (just clears extras; no surprise toast — the recipient didn't initiate this).

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 5 (Phase F — Bug #5: DSGVO Article 17 cascade for account deletion)
### Task Completed: F-DSGVO-DELETE-CASCADE — full per-user cloud cascade in `FirebaseSyncManager.deleteAllForUser`, awaited by `SettingsDialogFragment.performFirebaseDelete` BEFORE `FirebaseUser.delete()`

### Layer: Phase F (functional / legal-compliance). DEFERRED_ISSUES.md #2 + #23 (companion race condition). User-facing symptom: user taps "Delete account" in Settings → photo Storage gets cleaned up (fire-and-forget), local DB rows for plants/reminders/photos/auth wiped → `user.delete()` runs → auth account vanishes → BUT seven cloud subcollections remain: plants, reminders, rooms, memos, vacation, gamification/streak, gamification/challenges, billing/proStatus. After `user.delete()` they are unreachable to anyone (Firestore rules require `request.auth.uid == userId` and that uid is now deleted) but persist on Google's servers attached to the deleted account's PII. Direct DSGVO Article 17 (Right to Erasure) violation for the German market.

### Bug:

| Tag | File(s) | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-DSGVO-DELETE-CASCADE** | `FirebaseSyncManager.java` (added `deleteAllForUser` + `deleteAllDocsInCollection` helper + `DeleteAllForUserCallback` interface), `SettingsDialogFragment.java` (rewrote `performFirebaseDelete` to await the cascade) | **DSGVO violation: incomplete cloud cleanup on account deletion** | Pre-fix `performFirebaseDelete` called `FirebaseSyncManager.get().deleteAllPhotosForUser(email)` and immediately moved on — that method is fire-and-forget (no `Task` returned, no await). Then it deleted local rows for reminders/plants/photos/auth and called `user.delete()`. Net result: photos *might* finish cleaning up if the network was fast enough, but the seven other per-user subcollections (plants, reminders, rooms, memos, vacation, gamification/streak, gamification/challenges, billing/proStatus) were NEVER touched. Once `user.delete()` succeeded, Firestore rules (`request.auth.uid == userId` per `match /users/{userId}/{document=**}`) blocked any future cleanup attempt because the auth uid no longer existed. PII (plant nicknames, personal notes, watering schedules, journal memos, vacation date ranges, billing receipts) sat orphaned on Google's servers indefinitely. |

### Fix:

**Part 1 — new cascade method in `FirebaseSyncManager`:**

Added a new public callback interface (`DeleteAllForUserCallback { onComplete(boolean success) }`), a private helper (`deleteAllDocsInCollection(CollectionReference) -> Task<Void>`) that lists + deletes every doc in a subcollection via `Tasks.whenAll`, and the public method `deleteAllForUser(callback)` that fans out to ALL nine per-user cloud locations:

| # | Cloud location | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `users/{uid}/plants/*` (Firestore) | doc.delete() per plant |
| 1b | `users/{uid}/plants/{id}/cover.jpg` (Storage) | best-effort `coverRef.delete()`, swallowed-failure-wrapped (404 on plants without cover is normal) |
| 2 | `users/{uid}/reminders/*` | helper |
| 3 | `users/{uid}/photos/*` (Firestore) | doc.delete() per photo |
| 3b | Photo Storage originals | fire-and-forget via existing `deletePhotoSmart(p, null)` (no Task return; Firestore doc delete is what we await for the success flag) |
| 4 | `users/{uid}/rooms/*` | helper |
| 5 | `users/{uid}/memos/*` | helper |
| 6 | `users/{uid}/vacation/current` | single-doc delete |
| 7 | `users/{uid}/gamification/streak` | single-doc delete |
| 8 | `users/{uid}/gamification/challenges` | single-doc delete |
| 9 | `users/{uid}/billing/proStatus` | single-doc delete |

All sub-tasks are gathered into one `Tasks.whenAll` and the callback fires exactly once after every operation has settled. Firestore's "delete a non-existent doc is a no-op success" semantics mean single-doc deletes don't need failure-swallowing wrappers — only Storage cover deletes do (where 404 is the common case for plants without covers).

**Part 2 — rewrite `performFirebaseDelete`:**

The pre-fix sequence was `runIO { fire-and-forget photo delete + local DB wipes } -> user.delete()`. The new sequence is `cloud cascade (awaited) -> runIO { local DB wipes } -> user.delete()`. Same `FragmentBg.runIO` pattern is preserved for the local block — only the surrounding orchestration changed:

```java
FirebaseSyncManager.get().deleteAllForUser(cascadeOk -> {
    if (!cascadeOk) {
        CrashReporter.INSTANCE.log(new RuntimeException(
            "performFirebaseDelete: cloud cascade reported partial failure — proceeding with auth delete anyway"));
    }
    FragmentBg.runIO(this,
        () -> { /* local DB wipes — unchanged */ },
        () -> user.delete().addOnCompleteListener(t -> { /* finishDelete or toast — unchanged */ }));
});
```

Failure semantics: if the cascade reports `success=false` (any sub-task failed — typically a transient network drop), we log to Crashlytics and proceed with `user.delete()` anyway. The reasoning is documented inline:
- Half-deleted is still a DSGVO improvement over the pre-fix "fully orphaned" outcome.
- Once `user.delete()` succeeds, the user can't authenticate to retry the failed sub-deletions — so refusing to proceed would lock them out of completing the deletion forever.
- The pre-fix behavior was effectively "always proceed regardless of cloud state" — we keep that survivability while massively widening what gets cleaned up first.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 4 (Phase F — Bug #4: guest-row PK collision on sign-in)
### Task Completed: F-CLOUD-IMPORT-GUEST-PK-COLLISION — re-key guest plants + children before cloud import via marker-bumped autogen offset, then sync the promoted rows to Firestore

### Round-4 extension (2026-05-14, same day, same session):
A self-audit between rounds caught a NEW data-loss vector introduced by the original round-4 fix: promoted plants live only in the local DB (DAO insert bypasses cloud sync). On a subsequent sign-out/sign-in cycle the wipe step at the start of `importCloudDataForUser` deletes WHERE `userEmail = email` — which now includes the promoted plants — and cloud restore brings back nothing because they were never pushed. Net effect: guest data preserved on first sign-in, lost forever on the second.

Fix extension: after the local re-key transaction commits, push every promoted Plant + WateringReminder + JournalMemo to Firestore via `FirebaseSyncManager.{syncPlant, syncReminder, syncJournalMemo}` (per-row try/catch, fire-and-forget — Firebase's offline persistence queues writes when offline). This is done OUTSIDE `runInTransaction` so a Room rollback doesn't leave orphan cloud writes.

Implementation detail: collect `promotedPlants` / `promotedReminders` / `promotedMemos` in three `final` lists during the transaction lambda, then iterate them after commit. Set `gp.id = newId` immediately after `plantDao.insert(gp)` so the post-transaction Firebase calls reference the persisted id (Room doesn't auto-write the autogen result back to the entity for `int` PKs).

Photos remain intentionally cloud-unsynced — Storage upload requires resolving the local Uri and follows a different state machine (`uploadPlantPhotoWithPending`). The local photo entity is re-keyed correctly so the photo survives the first sign-in, but a second sign-out/sign-in cycle wipes the entity and the on-disk JPEG becomes an orphan. Tracked as a known follow-up.
### Layer: Phase F (functional). DEFERRED_ISSUES.md #5. User-facing symptom: guest user adds plants → signs in to a cloud account → cloud plants with overlapping ids are silently dropped (PlantDao default `OnConflictStrategy.ABORT` swallowed by per-row try/catch). Same loss for `WateringReminder` and `JournalMemo` (both ABORT). `PlantPhotoDao` is `REPLACE` so the cloud photo overwrites the guest photo — cloud wins for photos but the guest copy is destroyed.

### Deferred-issue premise correction:
DEFERRED #5 said *"guest rows have userEmail IS NULL"*. This is **stale**. The current implementation (`AuthRepository.kt:184` + `OnboardingActivity.kt:135` via `EmailContext.setCurrent(GUEST_EMAIL, true)`) sets `userEmail = "guest@local"` on every guest-created row. The fix targets that string literal explicitly — NULL handling intentionally out of scope (no current code path produces it; legacy migration would be a separate, narrower task).

### Bug:

| Tag | File | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-CLOUD-IMPORT-GUEST-PK-COLLISION** | `MainActivity.java` `importCloudDataForUser` (between the wipe step at line ~820-867 and the fan-out at line ~907) | **Silent cloud-data loss on guest→user transition** | The pre-fix wipe (`deleteAllUserPlantsForUserBlocking(email)`, etc.) clears rows where `userEmail = newEmail` — guest rows with `userEmail = "guest@local"` are intentionally untouched so the user keeps their guest data. But `Plant.id` is `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (verified in `app/schemas/com.example.plantcare.AppDatabase/16.json`), and cloud restore re-inserts plants with their cloud-side ids. If a guest plant happens to occupy the same id as an incoming cloud plant, `PlantDao @Insert` (default ABORT) throws `SQLiteConstraintException`, the surrounding `try { ... } catch (Throwable __ce) { ... }` swallows it, and the cloud row is dropped. Same risk for `ReminderDao` + `JournalMemoDao`; `PlantPhotoDao` (REPLACE) overwrites the guest photo with the cloud one — cloud wins but guest data is still lost. |

### Fix:

A new private static helper `promoteGuestRowsToUser(Context, String newEmail)` runs synchronously on the BgExecutor.io thread, AFTER the existing wipe step and BEFORE the 9-stream fan-out (line 902). Strategy:

1. **Bail-out fast** — return immediately if `newEmail` is null/empty/equal to `"guest@local"`, or if there are no guest plants. Most signed-in users never used guest mode → this is the common case and the helper costs ~one DB query.
2. **Bump SQLite's `AUTOINCREMENT` high-water mark** to a safe offset (1,000,000). We do this by inserting a throwaway marker plant at `id = REKEY_AUTOGEN_OFFSET` and immediately deleting it. SQLite's `sqlite_sequence` retains the high-water mark even after deletion (per `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` semantics), so subsequent autogen inserts begin at 1,000,001+ — comfortably above any realistic cloud plant id.
3. **Re-key each guest plant** in a loop. For each:
   - Snapshot child rows (Reminder / Photo / Memo) by the old `plantId`.
   - Insert a copy of the plant with `id = 0` (autogen) and `userEmail = newEmail`. Capture the new id.
   - Update each child to point at the new plant id and adopt the new email.
   - Delete the original guest plant. FK CASCADE matches no rows because every child was already migrated to the new id.
4. **Wrap the whole thing in `db.runInTransaction { ... }`** so observers see only the final state (no marker flicker), and a mid-loop failure rolls back cleanly without partial migration. FK enforcement stays ON throughout — the order (insert new parent → update children → delete old parent) satisfies the constraints at every step, no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` gymnastics needed.

Why this approach over the alternatives:
- **Option B (hard reset — delete guest data on sign-in)** is what Notion/Todoist do but is destructive and the user explicitly authorized "اعطيك الاذن" without specifying. Option A is non-destructive and user-respecting.
- **Raw SQL renumber + FK disable** would work but is fragile (PRAGMA scope, connection-pool surprises) and harder to reason about than a typed Kotlin/Java loop.
- **Re-key AFTER cloud import** would already have lost the cloud rows by then — they fail-fast on insert with the stale guest ids still in place.

Why 1,000,000 as the offset:
- Cloud plants typically use ids in the range 1-10,000 (per-account autogen). 1M is conservative — would only collide if a single user managed 1M+ plants on a single account. Vanishingly unlikely; if it ever surfaces, raise the offset.
- Plant.id is `int` so the maximum is ~2.1 B; we have headroom.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 3 (Phase F — Bug #3: FK race during cloud import)
### Task Completed: F-CLOUD-IMPORT-FK-RACE — two-phase ordering via CountDownLatch in `MainActivity.importCloudDataForUser`
### Layer: Phase F (functional). DEFERRED_ISSUES.md #4. User-facing symptom: reinstall on a new device → restore from cloud → user sees ~90% of their data with random gaps in reminders / photos / memos. Cause is silent FK CASCADE rejection of child rows that arrived before their parent Plant landed in the local DB.

### Bug:

| Tag | File | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-CLOUD-IMPORT-FK-RACE** | `MainActivity.java` lines 869-1126 (`importCloudDataForUser`) | **Silent data loss on cloud restore** | All 9 import streams ran in parallel on `BgExecutor.io` (a 4-thread shared pool). Three of them — `WateringReminder`, `PlantPhoto`, `JournalMemo` — declare `@ForeignKey(parentColumns="id", childColumns="plantId", onDelete=CASCADE)` to `Plant`. If a child stream's IO callback won the schedule and tried to insert before `onPlantsImported` had finished, Room rejected the insert with `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY` and the surrounding `try { ... } catch (Throwable __ce) { CrashReporter.INSTANCE.log(__ce); }` silently dropped the row. Pre-fix grep evidence: `grep -n "remaining.decrementAndGet" MainActivity.java` → 9 sites, all firing in parallel with no inter-stream synchronization. Probability of hit grows with account size: 5 plants → maybe never; 50+ plants → almost certainly partial loss on every restore. |

### Fix:

Two-phase ordering via a single `java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch(1)` named `plantsLatch`:

1. **Declared** at line 901 inside the existing `BgExecutor.io` block, alongside the existing `AtomicInteger remaining`.
2. **`onPlantsImported.finally`** — releases the latch (`plantsLatch.countDown()`) BEFORE decrementing `remaining`. Always fires, even on empty list or mid-loop exception.
3. **3 child callbacks** (`onRemindersImported`, `onPhotosImported`, `importMemosForCurrentUser`) — each calls a new private static helper `awaitPlantsLatch(plantsLatch)` BEFORE their for-loop. The helper waits up to 30 s, logs to Crashlytics on timeout, and proceeds (children FK-fail individually as pre-fix — no worse than today).
4. **Outer-failure `catch (Throwable t)`** — defensively counts the latch down so any callback that managed to register before the throw doesn't sit on its 30 s await.

The 6 independent streams (ProStatus, Streak, Challenges, Vacation, Rooms, Plants itself) keep running in parallel — only the 3 child callbacks now gate on Plants. `remaining = 9` and the 9 `decrementAndGet` sites are unchanged; `onCloudImportFinished` still fires when all streams finish.

Why a latch and not a coroutine refactor: minimal diff in a Java callback-based hotspot (~15 lines added, 0 lines deleted excluding comments). The 30 s timeout is the explicit safety net — if Plants never arrives (Firestore SDK glitch / network drop), we degrade to pre-fix behavior, never deadlock the import.

Why not also gate on Rooms: `Plant.roomId` is a plain `int` column with NO `@ForeignKey` constraint. A plant inserted before its room shows in "no room" until the room arrives — UX wart, not data loss. Out of scope for the FK-race fix.

### Verification (static — sandbox can't run gradle, no SDK / no network for Gradle 8.12 wrapper):

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Latch declared exactly once | `grep -n "CountDownLatch plantsLatch\|new java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch(1)" MainActivity.java` | 1 declaration, lines 901-902 ✅ |
| `countDown()` called exactly twice (plants finally + outer catch) | `grep -n "plantsLatch.countDown" MainActivity.java` | 2 hits: line 1059 (`onPlantsImported.finally`), line 1123 (outer `catch`) ✅ |
| `awaitPlantsLatch(plantsLatch)` called exactly thrice (3 children) | `grep -n "awaitPlantsLatch(plantsLatch)" MainActivity.java` | 3 hits: line 1014 (memos), 1071 (reminders), 1094 (photos) ✅ |
| Helper method defined | `grep -n "private static void awaitPlantsLatch" MainActivity.java` | 1 hit, line 1139 ✅ |
| `AtomicInteger remaining` unchanged | `grep -n "AtomicInteger remaining" MainActivity.java` | still `new AtomicInteger(9)` ✅ |
| `decrementAndGet` count unchanged (still 9 — one per stream) | `grep -c "remaining.decrementAndGet" MainActivity.java` | 9 ✅ |
| File still parses (visual brace balance + braces around lambdas) | re-read 1109-1148 | ok ✅ |

### Build Status: ⏳ deferred to local machine — sandbox can't reach `services.gradle.org`. Run `./gradlew :app:assembleProdRelease` locally; round 2 (Bug #7) edit needs the same build pass.

### Regressions:
- No public API change (helper is `private static`).
- No schema change.
- No new dependencies (everything from `java.util.concurrent`).
- 6 independent streams unchanged in behavior.
- The 3 child callbacks add a single `awaitPlantsLatch(...)` line at the top of their try block — the for-loops, repository calls, FK behavior, and `try/catch (__ce)` per-row swallow are byte-identical to pre-fix.
- `onPlantsImported` now does one extra `plantsLatch.countDown()` in its finally — costs a CAS, irrelevant.
- Outer catch does one extra defensive `countDown()` — same.

### Behavior change to verify on device:
Reinstall scenario (the original symptom):
1. Sign in on Device A, add 50+ plants with reminders + photos + memos.
2. Wait ~30 s for cloud sync.
3. Uninstall the app on Device A (or factory-reset).
4. Reinstall, sign in with the same account.
5. **Pre-fix:** Today list and plant detail screens show random gaps — some plants have no reminders, some have no archive photos, some have no memos.
6. **Post-fix:** All plants have their full reminder schedule + photo archive + memo timeline restored.

For a smaller account (5-10 plants) the bug rarely manifests — the timing window is too tight. The fix is most visible on larger accounts (50+ plants).

### Pre-existing issue acknowledged but NOT touched in this round:
The outer `catch (Throwable t)` at line 1111 lifts `CLOUD_IMPORT_IN_PROGRESS` and now releases the latch, but it does NOT decrement `remaining` — so if the throw happens after some streams registered but before others, `remaining` may never hit 0 and `onCloudImportFinished` may never fire. This is unchanged from pre-fix behavior. Real impact is small (the worst case is a stale ProgressDialog that doesn't auto-dismiss, but there is no ProgressDialog in this code path), but worth tracking. Add a follow-up entry if you want it tightened.

## Session: 2026-05-14 round 2 (Phase F — Bug #7: watering interval lying-save)
### Task Completed: F-EDIT-WATERIV-LYING-SAVE — fixed in EditPlantDialogFragment.saveChanges
### Layer: Phase F (functional). User-reported "lying save": every other Pflege-Plan input persists correctly except `Gießen` — change → Speichern → toast "Gespeichert" → re-open → value reverted. Brief: `Cowork_Brief_WateringInterval_Bug.md` (root) §3 root cause, §5 Option A recommended.

### Bug:

| Tag | File | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-EDIT-WATERIV-LYING-SAVE** | `EditPlantDialogFragment.java` lines 212-223 | **Lying save** | `saveChanges()` had asymmetric save logic: only the watering branch ran a `parsedFromText > 0 ? parsedFromText : readInterval(...)` short-circuit. `parseWateringInterval` is a naive last-int grabber — for the unchanged catalog text "Alle 14 Tage. Wenig Wasser genügt." it returns 14. So a user clearing the numeric `Gießen` field, typing `7`, hitting Speichern, saw a "Gespeichert" toast and the value silently reverting to 14 on next open. The text-priority branch was added (per the original comment) so a description edit "Alle 14 Tage" → "Alle 7 Tage" would auto-reschedule, but round-5's `prefillInterval` already covers that flow by pre-filling the numeric field with the parsed/derived value when the stored interval is 0 — so the description-edit case is now handled in the prefill, no save-time override needed. |

### Fix:

Option A from the brief (recommended): drop the text-parse priority branch entirely. The four interval fields now all use the same `readInterval(field, fallback)` path with the old value as fallback — symmetric with Düngen / Sprühen / Umtopfen. The prefill from round-5 still derives a parsed value from the description text when the plant has no stored interval, so users editing a fresh catalog plant still see "Alle 14 Tage" rendered as `14` in the numeric field — they can accept it (numeric stays 14) or override (type 7 → save → 7 sticks). The user can still empty any field to explicitly disable that reminder type — `readInterval` returns 0 for blank input, which the regenerate logic treats as "skip this reminder type".

Diff is small: 9 lines removed (the text-parse branch + its old comment) + 27 lines added (the new explanatory comment + the now-symmetric `final int newWaterIv = readInterval(...)` line). Net change in `saveChanges`: `parsedFromText` local + ternary disappear; `newWaterIv` becomes a single `readInterval(editIntervalWater, oldWaterIv)` call. No new helpers, no schema change, no behaviour change for the other three intervals.

### Verification:

**Static checks (sandbox can't run gradle — no Android SDK, no internet for Gradle 8.12 wrapper download — build verification deferred to Fady's local machine):**

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `parseWateringInterval` no longer called from save path | `grep -n parseWateringInterval app/src/main/java/com/example/plantcare/EditPlantDialogFragment.java` | 1 hit at line 220 — only inside the explanatory comment, not a live call ✅ |
| All four interval reads now symmetric | `grep -nE "newWaterIv\|newFertIv\|newMistIv\|newRepotIv" .../EditPlantDialogFragment.java \| grep readInterval` | 4 hits (lines 235-238), all `readInterval(editIntervalX, oldXIv)` ✅ |
| `parseWateringInterval` still legitimately used elsewhere | `grep -rn parseWateringInterval app/src/main/java` | 8 hits across 7 files: `AddPlantDialogFragment`, `AllPlantsFragment`, `PlantCatalogLookup`, `PlantIdentifyActivity`, `QuickAddHelper`, `ReminderUtils` (definition), `PlantCareDefaults` (Kotlin doc reference), and the 1 comment in `EditPlantDialogFragment` ✅ — function not orphaned, definition stays |
| Imports still all in use | `grep -n "^import" .../EditPlantDialogFragment.java`; verified `TextUtils.isEmpty` at line 185 (name validation) and `ReminderUtils.parseIntervalDays` at line 145 + `generateAllReminders` at line 278 | no orphans ✅ |

### Build Status: ⏳ deferred — sandbox cannot reach `services.gradle.org` to fetch the Gradle wrapper. Fady to run `./gradlew :app:assembleProdRelease` locally.

### Regressions: none expected.
- No public API changed.
- No schema change.
- No new dependencies.
- The other three intervals (Düngen / Sprühen / Umtopfen) are unchanged — their `readInterval(field, oldXIv)` path is the one the watering field now joins.
- Round-5's `prefillInterval` + `derivedInterval` helpers are untouched and still pre-populate the numeric field for catalog plants — the description-edit-only flow is now handled at prefill time instead of save time.
- `parseWateringInterval` (the function itself) is unchanged and still used legitimately by 6 other call sites that parse catalog text on initial plant insert (where the description IS the only source of truth — no numeric field exists yet).

### Trade-off acknowledged:
A user who edits ONLY the description text (e.g. changes "Alle 14 Tage" → "Alle 7 Tage" in the free-text `Bewässerung` field) and leaves the numeric field at 14 will keep the 14-day cadence. Mitigation: the prefill makes the canonical numeric source visible — a user editing a description string while the matching number is right next to it has a clear visual cue. Per the brief, this is the trade Option A consciously makes for symmetry + zero "lying save" risk.

### Tasks Completed: 6 fixes from on-device testing (F-AUTH-GOOGLE, F-AUTH-APPLE-REMOVE, F-AUTH-MAGICLINK-REMOVE, F-AUTH-ENTRY-DIFF, F-AUTH-BUTTONS-UNIFY, F-EDIT-PFLEGEPLAN)
### Layer: Phase F (functional). User report from `~/Downloads/PlantCare ScreenShots/Screenshot_20260513_2112*.png` after the G-SWITCH fixes landed.

### Bug catalog:

| Tag | File(s) | Type | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-AUTH-GOOGLE** | `AuthStartDialogFragment.java` | **Broken flow** | Google account chooser shows, user picks an account, nothing happens — no Firebase session, no toast, no inline error. Two root causes in code: (1) `registerForActivityResult` was called from `onCreateDialog` instead of `onCreate`, which on some devices means the result callback never fires (Android docs require registration before STARTED). (2) Both the OneTap and Legacy launchers handled `RESULT_CANCELED` with a silent `setLoading(false)` — no user-visible feedback when a SHA-1 cert mismatch / Play Services error cancelled the chooser. |
| **F-AUTH-APPLE-REMOVE** | `dialog_auth_start.xml`, `AuthStartDialogFragment.java` | **Wrong platform** | "Mit Apple anmelden" button visible on an Android-only app for the German market — Apple Sign-In is iOS/web only and the helper class can't authenticate on Android without a server round-trip we don't run. |
| **F-AUTH-MAGICLINK-REMOVE** | `dialog_auth_start.xml`, `AuthStartDialogFragment.java` | **Broken flow** | "Anmeldelink per E-Mail" sends a Firebase email-link but the return Deep Link (`https://com.fadymerey.plantcare.firebaseapp.com/finishSignIn`) requires Firebase Dynamic Links + an `intent-filter android:autoVerify="true"` — neither configured. The class `AuthMagicLink` stays in the codebase so MainActivity's `finishFromIntent` defensive handler still works if a user has an old pending link; only the UI entry point is removed. |
| **F-AUTH-ENTRY-DIFF** | `OnboardingActivity.kt`, `MainActivity.java`, `AuthStartDialogFragment.java` | **UX bug** | Onboarding's "Konto erstellen" and "Anmelden" buttons both called `startActivity(MainActivity, "show_auth"=true)`, and MainActivity ignored the extra and always opened AuthStart in the same neutral state. So both buttons rendered the same dialog — login and register pathways were indistinguishable. |
| **F-AUTH-BUTTONS-UNIFY** | `dialog_auth_start.xml` | **Visual inconsistency** | First three buttons (Google / Apple / Email) were 48 dp MaterialButtons; "Schon ein Konto? Hier anmelden" was a left-aligned TextView, "Anmeldelink per E-Mail" was a 40 dp MaterialButton.Text — three different shapes/heights in one dialog. |
| **F-EDIT-PFLEGEPLAN** | `EditPlantDialogFragment.java` | **Empty UI** | Opening a catalog plant from "Alle Pflanzen" → Bearbeiten showed four EMPTY input boxes next to Gießen / Düngen / Sprühen / Umtopfen, although `dialog_plant_detail` clearly displayed "Alle 14 Tage" etc. above. Root cause: catalog rows from `plants.csv` (via `CatalogSeeder`) only populate the descriptive text fields — `wateringInterval` / `fertilizingInterval` / `mistingInterval` / `repottingIntervalDays` stay at schema default 0, and `prefillInterval` rendered 0 as blank. |

### Fixes:

**F-AUTH-GOOGLE** — Lifecycle + visible error feedback in `AuthStartDialogFragment.java`

- Moved `resolveWebClientId()` / `setupGoogleIdentityLauncher()` / `setupGoogleLegacyLauncher()` from `onCreateDialog` to `onCreate(Bundle)`. The two `registerForActivityResult` calls now happen before the fragment hits STARTED — per Google's docs this is the only safe ordering for result callbacks after process death / config change.
- Split the previous combined `setupGoogleIdentity` into `configureGoogleSignInRequests` (cheap object building, still runs from `onCreateDialog`) + `setupGoogleIdentityLauncher` (one-shot launcher registration, runs from `onCreate`). Same for the legacy path.
- OneTap launcher `RESULT_CANCELED` branch now falls back to the legacy chooser when available; if the legacy fallback also fails it shows a new persistent inline error `R.string.auth_google_cancelled`. The previous behaviour silently set `loading=false` and gave the user no clue what happened.
- Legacy launcher `RESULT_CANCELED` branch also shows the same inline error.
- Legacy `ApiException` branch now surfaces the numeric statusCode in the error text (most commonly `10 = DEVELOPER_ERROR`, which signals a SHA-1 mismatch — useful diagnostic during install testing).
- `startOneTap` first attempt is now `signInRequest` (filterByAuthorizedAccounts=true) for returning users; on failure falls through to `signUpRequest` automatically, then legacy. Pre-fix always started with `signUpRequest` which can surprise existing users with a fresh chooser.

**F-AUTH-APPLE-REMOVE** + **F-AUTH-MAGICLINK-REMOVE**

- `dialog_auth_start.xml`: removed `@+id/btnApple` and `@+id/btnMagicLink`.
- `AuthStartDialogFragment.java`: removed all `btnApple` / `btnMagicLink` wiring + the `showMagicLinkDialog()` private method (it built an in-code AlertDialog with an unstyled `EditText` that was hard to read against the dark theme anyway).
- Kept `AuthMagicLink.kt` + `AuthAppleSignIn.kt` so the codebase still compiles — `MainActivity.onCreate` line 105 still calls `AuthMagicLink.finishFromIntent` as a defensive handler for old pending links. When Dynamic Links is configured in a later release we can re-add the button without touching the lib classes.

**F-AUTH-ENTRY-DIFF** — Differentiated entry mode end-to-end

- New public consts `AuthStartDialogFragment.MODE_REGISTER` and `MODE_LOGIN`.
- New factory `AuthStartDialogFragment.newInstance(String mode)` stores the mode in the args bundle; `onCreate` reads it back so it survives rotation.
- `btnEmail` text now follows the mode: "Mit E-Mail registrieren" in REGISTER mode, new `R.string.auth_button_email_login` ("Mit E-Mail anmelden") in LOGIN mode. Clicking `btnEmail` opens `LoginDialogFragment` in the matching mode.
- The previous `textHaveAccount` TextView became `buttonToggleMode` (MaterialButton.Text full-width); its text inverts the mode ("Schon ein Konto? Hier anmelden" in REGISTER mode, "Neu hier? Jetzt registrieren" in LOGIN mode) and tapping opens `LoginDialogFragment` in the opposite mode.
- `OnboardingActivity.kt`: `btnCreateAccount` adds `auth_mode = MODE_REGISTER` to the MainActivity Intent; `btnLogin` adds `MODE_LOGIN`.
- `MainActivity.java`: reads the extra and routes through `AuthStartDialogFragment.newInstance(requestedMode)` — defaults to REGISTER for cold launches without the extra (preserves the original behaviour for any caller that didn't pass `auth_mode`).

**F-AUTH-BUTTONS-UNIFY** — Three-button consistent shape

- After removing Apple + Magic Link the surviving controls are Google (outlined 48 dp) → Email (filled 48 dp) → Toggle (text 48 dp). All three now use the same `PlantCare.Button.*` family at the same height, full-width with the same 12 dp marginBottom rhythm. The previous narrow left-aligned TextView is gone.

**F-EDIT-PFLEGEPLAN** — Derive defaults when stored interval is 0

- New private helper `derivedInterval(String careText, int familyFallback)` in `EditPlantDialogFragment.java`. Calls `ReminderUtils.parseIntervalDays(careText)` first (e.g. "Alle 14 Tage. Wenig Wasser genügt" → 14, "Von Frühling bis Sommer alle 4 Wochen düngen" → 28), then falls back to the family default when the text yields nothing.
- `onViewCreated` now resolves a `PlantCareDefaults.CareTexts` for `plant.family` and uses it for the four prefill values: watering + fertilizing parse from the descriptive text first; mist + repot fall straight to the family defaults (CSV doesn't carry these fields).
- The user can still empty any input to explicitly disable that reminder type — the existing `readInterval(... fallback=...)` saves 0 only when the field is blank.

## Session: 2026-05-13 round 4 (Phase G — Switch disabled-state fix follow-up)
### Tasks Completed: 1 visibility regression caught during user verification (G-SWITCH-DISABLED)
### Layer: Phase G follow-up.

### Bug:
User confirmed round 3's fix worked for every Switch in Settings EXCEPT `switchBiometric`. Root cause: `SettingsDialogFragment.java:213` calls `switchBiometric.setEnabled(AuthBiometric.isAvailable(...))`. On devices without biometric hardware (or in the emulator), this evaluates to `false` → the switch is in **disabled** state, not just unchecked. The round-3 ColorStateList had `pc_outlineVariant` (#495350 dark / #BFC9C2 light) as the disabled fallback — in dark mode `#495350` is too close to `pc_surface` (#0B0F0E) to be visible.

### Fix:
Rewrote `pc_switch_thumb_tint.xml` and `pc_switch_track_tint.xml` to keep the **same hue** (pc_outline / pc_primary) for the disabled state but apply `android:alpha="0.5"` — disabled stays clearly visible while still signalling its state. `android:alpha` on ColorStateList items requires API 23+; minSdk=24 so safe.

New CSL:
```xml
<item android:state_checked="true" android:state_enabled="true" android:color="@color/pc_primary"/>
<item android:state_enabled="true" android:color="@color/pc_outline"/>
<item android:state_checked="true" android:alpha="0.5" android:color="@color/pc_primary"/>
<item android:alpha="0.5" android:color="@color/pc_outline"/>
```

Contrast in dark mode (#0B0F0E surface):
- Enabled OFF: pc_outline #8A938F → ~6.5:1 ✅
- Disabled OFF: pc_outline @ 50% alpha on #0B0F0E ≈ #45494A effective → ~3:1 ✅ (visible but dimmer)

### Verification:
- Build: `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 56s (and re-run at end-of-session: 27s, incremental).
- No layout/code changes — purely two color resource rewrites.
